newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan June trade gap drops to $184 mln.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan June trade gap drops to $184 mln.

text.p: Pakistan's trade deficit dropped to a provisional $184 million in June from $293 million in May, but increased from $124 million in June 1996, the Federal Bureau of Statistics said on Saturday.
Exports increased by 2.7 percent to a provisional $733 million in June from $714 million in May, but decreased by 34 percent compared to $1,110 million in June 1996.
Imports decreased by 8.9 percent to provisional $917 million from $1,007 million in May and by 25.7 pecent compared to $1,234 million in June 1996.

The trade gap in fiscal 1996/97 (July/June) rose to $3.37 billion from $3.1 billion in the year-ago period. The main items of exports during the year were cotton, cotton yarn, rice, leather and sports goods. The main items of imports were crude petroleum and its products, machinery, power generating machines and chemicals.
